disease_label_per_paper: Flare of rheumatoid arthritis after COVID-19 vaccination
presentation_summary: 55-year-old man with non-erosive seropositive rheumatoid arthritis in sustained remission for more than 2 years on upadacitinib developed acute right-knee pain and swelling 12 hours after the second BNT162b2 vaccine dose.
Nine days after the second dose, exam showed clinically significant right-knee swelling and warmth with pain on flexion and extension, without other joint tenderness, swelling, or erythema.

Ultrasound showed a moderate-to-large compressible hypoechoic suprapatellar effusion extending 5.2 cm deep to the quadriceps tendon, power Doppler signal, and a posterior-knee effusion consistent with popliteal cyst.
Arthrocentesis yielded 24 mL inflammatory-appearing effusion with synovial WBC 24,385 cells/uL and 62% neutrophils. CRP was 8.0 mg/L and ESR 39 mm/h.
Serologies, negative cultures/crystal exam, and response to intra-articular steroid are preserved as confirmatory or treatment/outcome context outside presentation ranking.
